name: Neohesperidin DC
aliases: E959, INS 959, neohesperidin DC, neohesperidin dihydrochalcone, NHDC
what_is: A high-intensity sweetener and flavour-modifying additive derived from a citrus flavonoid through chemical processing, identified in the EU as E959.
why_botia: It is obtained from a citrus compound and sweetens at very low concentrations, so very little is needed — the label does not say how much. It is also used to modify flavours, not only to sweeten. JECFA evaluated it in 2026 and set a temporary limit: a reproductive toxicity study is still missing, which JECFA has requested before making the limit definitive.
can_1: Detect E959, neohesperidin DC, neohesperidin dihydrochalcone and NHDC when declared.
can_2: Show the sweetener, flavour and E-number context for the detected term.
cannot_1: Calculate the concentration or total intake from the ingredient list.
cannot_2: Treat authorisation as proof of zero risk or the presence of E959 as proof of a harmful exposure.
